title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 32–34): Grothendieck is building a 'combinatorial approach to topology'. In it, M is a set of (multi)strata. It carries an incidence/order relation ⊴, a further structure 𝓛 (written 'ic' or 𝓛 in the transcriptions, probably an incidence or link datum) and a dimension function |·|. A 'figure' is a subset of M satisfying closure conditions. An 'atelier attenant à M' is a chosen family 𝔉 of admissible M-figures. On p.32 he introduces a distinguished subset M_c ⊂ M of 'compact' strata, a 'compactology'. The machine transcription reads 'convictologie' on p.32; this is surely 'compactologie'. He notes that M_c cannot reasonably be defined intrinsically from (M, ⊴, 𝓛, |·|). His example is an ordered interval that is not a segment: only points and closed intervals [a,b] should count as compact.

This page makes four points.
(1) A compactology lets one define, besides compact figures and finite figures, the 'locally finite' figures. These are presumably the figures meeting each compact piece in only finitely many strata, by analogy with locally finite CW or simplicial complexes.
(2) In practice only three ateliers are needed: finite figures, locally finite figures, and (if need be) all M-figures.
(3) NB: the compact figures form an atelier attached to M_c, a sub-object of M. It is not attached to M unless M_c = M.
(4) Hence the right technical framework is a 'donnée compactologique' (M, ⊴, 𝓛, |·|, M_c). This datum is simpler than an atelier attached to M, because M_c ∈ 𝔓(M) (a subset of M) whereas 𝔉 ∈ 𝔓(𝔓(M)) (a set of subsets of M).

This feeds into p.34's change of terminology: 'atelier' moves to M itself, 'magasin' is used for the family of figures, and M_c becomes the 'coeur de l'atelier'. The problem served is choosing foundational data for a combinatorial or stratified model of tame topology. The aim is to handle non-compact situations by a minimal extra datum (the compact strata) rather than by specifying the whole family of admissible figures.
errors: No mathematical error. The claim 'locally finite figures' is not given a definition on this page; the presumed definition (finite intersection with every compact figure) is an inference.
The claim that compact figures form an atelier attached to M_c but not to M (unless M_c = M) is consistent with the setup but left unproved.

ideas.what: Equip the combinatorial stratified datum with a distinguished subset of 'compact' strata (a compactology), which cannot be recovered from the incidence data alone.
ideas.modern_name: bornology / compactology (choice of compact or bounded parts); compact-support data on a stratified complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Waelbroeck and Buchwalter for 'compactologies' (1960s, functional analysis); Hogbe-Nlend for bornologies

ideas.what: Distinguish three ateliers: finite figures, locally finite figures, and all figures.
ideas.modern_name: finite vs locally finite vs arbitrary (infinite) complexes; compact support vs Borel–Moore type finiteness
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Whitehead, CW complexes; locally finite chains)

ideas.what: Replace the second-order datum 𝔉 ⊂ 𝔓(M) by the first-order datum M_c ⊂ M as the foundational structure.
ideas.modern_name: economy of foundational data (bornology generating admissible families)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 combinatorial-topology project (ateliers/magasins of multistrata) is a sketch toward the 'tame topology' foundations called for in the Esquisse. It adds a compactology datum M_c and builds finite, locally finite and compact figure-families from it. As far as is known, it was never developed or published.
missed.quote: le bon cadre de l'approche combinatoire de la topologie que je propose, est plutôt la notion de donnée compactologique (M, ⊴, 𝓛, |·|, M_c)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor but concrete design choice for combinatorial models of non-compact stratified spaces (compact core + locally finite extension). It is relevant to comparisons with o-minimal or exit-path combinatorial models, though the idea itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is foundational bookkeeping within an unpublished project. The notions (compact parts, locally finite complexes) are classical; the novelty is only the specific packaging in Grothendieck's 'atelier' framework.
transcription_corrections: 'région compactologique' is more likely 'donnée compactologique' (compare 'C'est une donnée plus simple' just after).
The last line should read 'car M_c ∈ 𝔓(M), et 𝔉 ∈ 𝔓(𝔓(M))' (power set symbols), not '𝔄(M)' / '𝔄/𝔄(M)'.
On the previous page, 'convictologie' should be 'compactologie'.
The marginal '(technique)' above 'bon cadre' appears to be an inserted qualifier ('le bon cadre technique').
